reply_text:
Everything that controls the loops is in one directory of apm-lean, `holes/labs/topology-contract/`, which is now pushed to `github.com/holtzermann17/apm-lean`. It's about 2,700 lines in total.

| File | What it controls |
|---|---|
| `topology-supervisor.sh` (383 lines) | Top level. Runs the build loop, restarts it after faults (up to 3 repairs), and escalates. Each of topo1–3 is one supervisor under systemd; the launch line is in `~/notes/closer/relaunch-loops.sh`. |
| `topology-build-loop.sh` (581 lines) | One iteration: pick the next row, send it to a Codex seat through Agency, collect the receipt, send it to an independent review seat, apply the verdict, commit. Before any work it checks the statement registry (`scripts/statement-registry.py`) and stops if a frozen statement has changed. |
| `build_step.bb` (1,160 lines) | The rules, i.e. how the ledger changes state. Which row runs next (`selected`: priority, then kind). What each receipt outcome does (go, done, stop, replan, pass, fail), including stop-after-two, multi-job programs, the new `:stopped` state, and banking lemmas when a review passes. Also the lemma graph and the `priorities` ranking the strategy checkpoints use. |
| `worklist_check.bb` (212 lines) | The checker. It runs before every ledger write and rejects a ledger that breaks a rule: cycles, "done" without a passed review, the author reviewing their own work, commits outside the row's allowed files, fixture hashes that don't match. |
| `work-prompt.md`, `review-prompt.md` | What the Codex seats are told: how to do the work and what a receipt must contain; for reviewers, what makes a pass or a fail. |
| `worklist.edn`, `worklist2.edn`, `worklist3.edn` | The data, one ledger per loop: every row, its state, dependencies, acceptance criteria and evidence, plus the lemma graph. |
| `test-loop.sh`, `test-rejected-receipt.sh`, `test_gate_receipts.bb` | Tests of the transition rules. They run without dispatching any agents. |

Two more things are relevant for Rob:
- **Statement registry:** `problems/STATEMENTS.json` with `scripts/statement-registry.py`. This stops the loops from proving a weakened version of a problem; a statement only changes through an outside grade and re-admission, as we did for t98A02.
- **Recent design changes:** `git log -- holes/labs/topology-contract/` shows them, and each commit message explains the incident behind it.

The directory's `README.md` is out of date. It still describes the very first seed and a single loop. I can rewrite it into a short overview of the structure above before you send Rob the link, if you'd like.
